JournalMode.doc: Connection-level journaling mode. Memory: in-memory only, no on-disk artifacts (used for ephemeral databases and tests). Delete: rollback-journal-mode equivalent — at COMMIT the database is serialized to a temp file and atomic-renamed over the main file (Phase 18.1 has no journal file; the rewrite IS the durability mechanism). Wal: write-ahead-log — at COMMIT, dirty pages flush as WAL frames and fsync (gated by SyncLevel). Truncate, Persist, Off variants from mainline are deferred.

PageImage.doc: Refcounted page byte buffer. Targets MAY back this with Rc<Vec<u8>>, Arc<[u8]>, refcounted slab, etc. The contract is: cheap to clone (no deep copy), exactly page_size bytes when materialized.

Pager.doc: Owns the page cache + WAL state + journal mode + sync level for a path-backed (or in-memory) Database. Threaded through every cursor mutation and read so the cursor consults the cache (which may fault from main file or WAL) instead of holding its own row clone. db_path is empty string for in-memory mode. wal is None unless journal_mode == Wal. lock holds the per-database lock state (process-local for v1; promoted to wal-shm-mediated in pin 20).

pager_new_in_memory.doc: Construct an in-memory Pager. db_path is empty, page_size is 4096 (default), cache has capacity 0 (degenerate; never holds pages — every pager_get_page returns an err since there's no on-disk source), wal is None, journal_mode = Memory, synchronous = Off. Used by Database::new() and by tests that want a Pager handle without I/O.

pager_new_file_backed.doc: Construct a file-backed Pager rooted at the given path. Reads the database header to determine page_size (defaults to 4096 if the file is empty or smaller than 100 bytes). Opens or creates the WAL via wal_open. Initializes a PageCache with capacity 2000. Default journal_mode = Wal, default synchronous = Normal. Returns err(IoError) if the path is unreadable or the header is corrupt.

pager_get_page.doc: Fetch a page image. Cache lookup (mutable: LRU touch on hit); on miss in Wal mode consults wal_read_page; on miss in any mode falls back to reading the main file at offset (page_no - 1) * page_size, then caches the result. Returns the cached/loaded image. Err on I/O failure or invalid page_no (zero or beyond file length AND beyond WAL). Borrow note: the parameter is `borrow_mut` because cache.get mutates the LRU order — page-cache pin 3 requires this. Read-only callers MUST still pass &mut Pager; this matches mainline's pager-borrow-mutably-on-every-call convention.

pager_get_page_mut.doc: Fetch a page image and mark it dirty in the cache. Equivalent to pager_get_page followed by pager_mark_dirty. Used by B-tree write paths.

pager_mark_dirty.doc: Set the dirty flag on a cached page. Err(IoError) if page_no is not present in the cache (caller must have faulted it via pager_get_page first).

pager_set_journal_mode.doc: Switch the connection's journal mode. Memory→Wal opens the WAL file; Wal→Memory drops the WAL state (unsafe if WAL has unflushed frames; caller's responsibility to checkpoint first). Memory→Delete and Delete→Wal are also valid transitions. Subsequent commits honor the new mode.

pager_set_synchronous.doc: Set the connection's synchronous level. Pure assignment; no side effects. Subsequent fsync sites (wal_commit, wal_checkpoint, atomic-rename commit) consult the new level.

pager_begin_transaction.doc: Mark the start of a transaction. In Wal mode this is a logical mark only — the writer lock is acquired lazily on first commit. In Delete mode this is a no-op (Delete commits with no preceding mark).

pager_commit_transaction.doc: Persist the database state per the journal mode. Memory: no-op. Delete: serialize Database to db_path via fileformat-write atomic-rename, fsync per synchronous. Wal (pin 19): the page cache is the source of truth — cursor write paths have already mutated page images in place via pager_get_page_mut. COMMIT acquires WalLockSlot::Write, calls cache.flush_dirty() to obtain the dirty set in ascending page_no order, appends each as a wal frame, then wal_commit (fsync per synchronous matrix). new_db_size for the commit frame == p.db_size_pages (the running total maintained by pager_allocate_page). Borrow note: this function reads the Database (for catalog inspection on rollback recovery) and mutates the Pager — callers MUST pass disjoint borrows via the borrow-split helper on Database.

pager_rollback_transaction.doc: Discard the in-progress transaction. Wal: wal_rollback (drop pending frames) + cache.clear (drop dirty in-memory pages) + release writer lock if held. Memory/Delete: no-op (mem-store v7-tx in-memory rollback handles row truncation).

pager_checkpoint.doc: Fold all committed WAL frames into the main database file and reset the WAL header (PASSIVE checkpoint per W8). No-op for non-Wal modes. Acquires WalLockSlot::Checkpoint exclusive; err(LockError::Busy) if another writer/checkpointer holds it.

pager_close.doc: Best-effort close: in Wal mode, attempt one passive checkpoint (silently skip on failure — the WAL replays on next open). Drop the cache and close the main file handle. Consumes the Pager.
